title: Nvidia Stock Plunges After Jensen Huang Resigns as CEO
text:
Supported by
Nvidia Shares Plunge, Shaking Up Tech Stocks
News that the chipmaker’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, stepped down drove Nvidia’s stock down and reverberated across global markets.
Nvidia’s share price
Nvidia’s shares plummeted Thursday, sending tremors through global markets, as the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, stepped down from his role.
Shares in Nvidia dropped more than 10 percent when markets opened for trading on Thursday, extending a drop that has wiped out more than $1 trillion from the company’s market value this month alone.
The company’s board named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as its interim chief executive.
With the change in Nvidia’s leadership, investors face uncertainty about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade and how the problems inside one of the technology industry’s most important companies could affect the broader economy.
The fallout could be seen in markets around the world, although the effects appeared limited. Major market indexes in Asia, where many of Nvidia’s partners and rivals in the artificial intelligence industry are based, mostly declined. Taiwan’s TSMC, which produces chips designed by Nvidia, fell nearly 2 percent. But South Korea’s Samsung, which competes with Nvidia on some business lines, gained 1 percent.
European stock indexes, which are less heavily exposed to A.I., were flat on Thursday. But shares in the region’s largest tech company, ASML of the Netherlands, fell nearly 2 percent.
